newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia nuclear arms systems decay, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Russia nuclear arms systems decay, minister says.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Thursday the country's armed forces were in such a "horrifying state" that the reliability of its nuclear weapons systems was in doubt, Interfax news agency said.

Rodionov, who outlined his fears in a letter to President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, suggested nuclear command and control centres were in decay because of a lack of funding.
"No one today can guarantee the reliability of our control systems," Interfax quoted him as saying.
"Russia might soon reach the threshold beyond which its rockets and nuclear systems cannot be controlled."
The comments were the latest shots in a battle which the 60-year-old minister has been waging over reforms and defence spending since he was appointed by Yeltsin last July.
The Russian media say differences among defence and security chiefs have prevented reforms getting off the drawing board.
"The whole horror is in the fact that, as Russian defence minister, I am becoming a spectator of the destructive processes in the army and can nothing about it," Rodionov said.

Interfax quoted Rodionov as saying Russia's combat readiness had been dropping constantly since 1990 and its weapons systems were falling into decay while the United States, Moscow's former Cold War foe, was improving its own systems.

Rodionov also said he was alarmed by the psychological frame of mind of many troops, especially officers. The number of suicides in the military, once minimal, had risen to about 100 in 1996, he said.

Rodionov is expected to give a news conference on Friday with Yuri Baturin, secretary of the Defence Council which is charged with overseeing military reforms. Russian media say they have clashed over reforms but they have played down the reports.
